raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a PD prefill server, `apply_cuda_graph_disaggregation_roles` resolves the decode graph phase to `Backend.DISABLED`. `capture_decode_graph` then returns before it constructs `current_platform.get_graph_runner_cls()`. For CUDA graphs that is correct, since a prefill server never replays decode graphs.

Some out-of-tree platforms use the graph runner as *the* compiled-execution owner. Their runner builds and serves the compiled prefill buckets as well as decode. On a PD prefill server such a platform ends up with no compiled prefill, or has to monkeypatch `ModelRunner.init_cuda_graphs` to build the runner anyway.

## Modifications

- New `PlatformCapabilities.graph_runner_owns_prefill: bool = False`. It means the platform's graph runner also builds and serves the compiled prefill path, so it must exist on a PD prefill server.
- `apply_cuda_graph_disaggregation_roles`: for `disaggregation_mode == "prefill"`, the decode phase is no longer forced to `DISABLED` when the capability is set. An explicit `--cuda-graph-backend-decode` still wins, as before.

In-tree platforms are unaffected: the capability defaults to False.

Users can already work around this per launch with `--cuda-graph-backend-decode full` on the prefill server. The capability makes it the platform's default, so a bare PD launch is correct.

## How it was found

Found while building an out-of-tree Neuron/Trainium platform plugin. Its graph runner warms and serves the compiled (NEFF) prefill and decode buckets. On PD prefill servers no runner was built, so the plugin now wraps `ModelRunner.init_cuda_graphs` to construct it after the fact. This capability would replace that wrapper.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. There is no behavior change for in-tree platforms.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

- Run (macOS, CPU only): `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py::TestCudaGraphDisaggregationRoles` has a new case: with a patched platform that sets the capability, the prefill role keeps the decode phase enabled. The existing cases (the default prefill role disables decode; an explicit decode backend survives) still pass.
- Across `test_server_args.py`, `test_platform_interface.py` and `test_resolution_is_reproducible.py`: 399 passed. 7 failed, but the same 7 fail on unmodified `main` in this environment (missing `lscpu` / optional packages on macOS).
- Not run: GPU or out-of-tree PD launch against this branch.

## Open questions

- Naming and placement: is a capability flag right, or should this be a platform method (e.g. `graph_runner_roles(disaggregation_mode)`)? Should it also stop the decode role from disabling the *prefill* phase, for symmetry? A runner that owns prefill should arguably not be told to skip it on decode servers either. I kept the change to the case I hit.
- `capture_decode_graph` also skips the target-verify graph on spec-decode PD prefill servers. That path is left unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
